Market is closed (block.closed_sessions includes us_equities_24/5): every stock mark is frozen at its last round while GeckoTerminal pools kept trading, so several divergence findings (AMZN -393.56bps, GOOGL +129.43bps, MSTR -424.05bps) reflect stale marks, not real moves. I'm reading co-movement off the 20-day daily-close timelines of the tradeable set, since that's the only apples-to-apples series across names.

The broad market (SPY, QQQ) has been flat to mildly soft over the window: SPY 766.13 -> 761.55 (-0.6%) [timeline 2026-08-21, timeline 2026-09-18], QQQ 713.79 -> 720.37 (+0.9%) [timeline 2026-08-21, timeline 2026-09-18]. Against that quiet macro tape, several single names in this book moved 2-5x the index magnitude in the same 20 days: AAPL +8.5% (308.94->335.38) [timeline 2026-08-21, timeline 2026-09-18], MU +4.8% (967.92->1014.43) [timeline], META +21.4% (549.15->666.76) [timeline], TSLA +0.4% (362.26->363.80) [timeline], NVDA +3.6% (214.71->222.45) [timeline], GME +23.8% (18.23->22.55) [timeline]. That spread — big single-stock dispersion against a nearly flat SPY/QQQ — says the book's risk is concentrated in idiosyncratic tech/AI names, not broad beta, and SPY/QQQ are the cleanest low-correlation ballast the book holds. USO moved with a distinct commodity path (+14.3%, 135.26->154.54) [timeline 2026-08-21, timeline 2026-09-18] uncorrelated to the equity moves, a genuine diversifier; SLV, the other commodity, is not tradeable this snapshot (below corroborator line) so I have no call there.

Within the tradeable names, META and GME/NVDA/MU all trended up together through the second half of the window (roughly 09-08 through 09-17), while AMZN drifted down over the same stretch (259->246 by 09-16) [timeline 2026-09-08, timeline 2026-09-16], the one clear divergence from the AI/tech cluster. That makes AMZN a partial hedge against the book's concentrated tech exposure rather than a repeat of it.

SPY was essentially flat over 30 days (766.13 -> 761.55, -0.6%) [timeline 2026-08-21, timeline 2026-09-18] while single names in the book (META +21%, GME +24%) swung far more; adding SPY diversifies a book whose realized moves are dominated by idiosyncratic tech bets.

The market is shut (`block.closed_sessions` includes us_equities_24/5): every mark is frozen at its last Chainlink round from before the close, while GeckoTerminal and the venue keep trading. That means divergence between mark and corroborator is expected background noise here, not automatically a mark failure — but it is still worth flagging where the gap is large and where mark and venue agree tightly against a stale-looking corroborator, or vice versa. I limit calls to `tradeable` assets, since the other nineteen are already priced off-book by the corroborator-line rule and not my call to relitigate.

Of the sixteen tradeable names, most show mark and venue within single-digit-to-low-double-digit bps of each other (AAPL, CRCL, NVDA, TSLA, GOOGL, SPCX, USO, MSFT-excluded etc.), which is the expected shape in a closed session: two independent readings (mark, venue) agree and the corroborator is the outlier or is itself thin/lagging. Three assets carry explicit closed-session divergence findings against GeckoTerminal beyond the 100bps open-session veto line: AMZN, GOOGL, MSTR. I look at these plus one more, AMD's neighbor set, for where the mark itself, not just staleness, looks suspect.

CALL AMZN 0x12f190a9f9d7d37a250758b26824b97ce941bf54 caution medium
Mark and venue agree closely, but GeckoTerminal sits far above both, well past what closed-session staleness alone should explain given AMZN's better-than-$1M corroborator volume.
- mark 253.863 vs venue 254.07317742977355, 0.08% apart [mark.price_usd, quote.venue_price_usd]
- GeckoTerminal 264.2631498551 on $1043579.83868448 24h volume [corroboration.price_usd, corroboration.volume_24h_usd]
- divergence -393.56 bps, flagged as beyond the open-session limit [corroboration.divergence_bps, findings]
Wrong if: GeckoTerminal's price converges back within 100bps of the mark once the market reopens, confirming it was just weekend pool drift on decent volume.

CALL GOOGL 0x2e0847e8910a9732eb3fb1bb4b70a580adad4fe3 caution medium
Same pattern as AMZN: mark and venue are close, corroborator has real volume ($4.77M) yet diverges 129bps, past the open-session veto threshold.
- mark 350.47135177 vs venue 352.2002869471623, 0.49% apart [mark.price_usd, quote.venue_price_usd]
- GeckoTerminal 345.9933348603 on $4769689.8474691 24h volume [corroboration.price_usd, corroboration.volume_24h_usd]
- divergence 129.43 bps, flagged beyond the open-session limit [corroboration.divergence_bps, findings]
Wrong if: the gap closes to within 100bps of the mark once trading resumes and the feed catches up.

CALL MSTR 0xec262a75e413fafd0df80480274532c79d42da09 caution medium
Mark and venue again tightly aligned (0.6% apart), but GeckoTerminal is 424bps below, the widest of the three flagged findings, on ample $3.4M volume — MSTR is volatile enough that a weekend pool move of this size is plausible but not confirmable from this snapshot alone.
- mark 152.643 vs venue 158.504043531346, 3.7% apart in the other direction from GeckoTerminal [mark.price_usd, quote.venue_price_usd]
- GeckoTerminal 159.4023510332 on $3426185.78320205 24h volume [corroboration.price_usd, corroboration.volume_24h_usd]
- divergence -424.05 bps, flagged beyond the open-session limit [corroboration.divergence_bps, findings]
Wrong if: GeckoTerminal and venue converge toward each other and the mark once the feed updates at open, showing this was weekend drift, not a stale/bad mark.

CALL NVDA 0xd0601ce157db5bdc3162bbac2a2c8af5320d9eec proceed high
All three prices agree tightly despite the closed session and high corroborator volume, so NVDA's mark holds up cleanly; noting this since NVDA carries the largest 24h volume of any asset here and is a useful sanity anchor for the batch.

- divergence 4.67 bps on $56212678.2164567 volume [corroboration.divergence_bps, corroboration.volume_24h_usd]
